title: Phase-sensitive quantum-state texture during thermalization of a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Heisenberg dimer
authors: Onofre Rojas, Zhirayr Adamyan, Fadwa Benabdallah, Vadim Ohanyan
abstract: We investigate quantum-state texture during the thermal relaxation of an anisotropic spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg dimer subject to a longitudinal magnetic field and a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. Starting from local transverse and longitudinal couplings to a bosonic bath, we construct a global weak-coupling Lindblad equation, identify its transition channels, and discuss the applicability and limitations of the secular approximation. The Gibbs state is obtained explicitly in the local spin basis, revealing that the DM coupling controls both the modulus and phase of the single-excitation coherence by modifying the energy splitting and rotating the chiral phase. For heating and cooling protocols, we compare rugosity, fidelity-based texture, and trace-distance texture with coherence, vector spin chirality, and purity. The relaxation dynamics separates population thermalization from the decay and precession of deliberately prepared energy-basis coherence. Their combined contribution to local coherence produces DM-dependent texture overshoots and, during cooling, damped oscillations and sign changes of the coherence quadratures. These transients differ from the evolution of coherence magnitude and purity, while trace-distance texture weights them differently from the overlap-based quantifiers. Calculations at reduced dissipation preserve the texture maxima within the secular model. The results identify a phase-sensitive diagnostic of relaxation.
summary: This paper analyzes how quantum-state texture evolves as an anisotropic Heisenberg dimer thermalizes. By solving the Lindblad master equation, the authors show that the DM interaction imparts a phase-sensitive signature on this texture. This demonstrates that texture is a powerful diagnostic tool, revealing complex dynamics distinct from simple population decay.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex dynamics of quantum-state texture during the thermal relaxation process of an anisotropic spin-1/2 Heisenberg dimer.
main_result: The research establishes that quantum-state texture serves as a phase-sensitive diagnostic of thermal relaxation, revealing distinct transient behaviors during cooling and heating protocols.
method: The authors construct and solve a global weak-coupling Lindblad master equation, comparing various texture diagnostics (like rugosity and fidelity) against standard measures like purity.
model_or_system: The system is an anisotropic spin-1/2 Heisenberg dimer subjected to a longitudinal magnetic field and a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. The dynamics are modeled using the Lindblad formalism coupled to a bosonic bath.
key_observables: Quantum-state texture (diagnosed by rugosity, fidelity-based texture, trace-distance texture), single-excitation coherence, vector spin chirality, and purity.
important_parameters: The DM coupling strength (D), the longitudinal field (h), and the temperature/thermal bath parameters ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Born–Markov approximation and the full secular approximation for the weak-coupling regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of purity and texture measures during heating and cooling protocols for varying DM coupling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper first sets up the Hamiltonian and the Lindblad master equation, then analyzes the separation of population thermalization from coherence decay, and finally compares various texture diagnostics to show the phase-sensitive nature of the relaxation.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, quantitative look at non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, specifically highlighting how geometric/phase information (texture) survives and characterizes relaxation beyond simple measures of mixedness.
